perf.summary: Separate sin/cos and a divide that can be a reciprocal-multiply
perf.currentCost: len = math.length(axis); n = axis/len does a float3 divide (3 divides via vector div); then math.sin(halfAngle) and math.cos(halfAngle) are two separate transcendental calls.
perf.proposedChange: Use math.sincos(halfAngle, out float s, out float c) for one combined evaluation. Replace axis/len with axis * (One/len) so the per-component operation is a multiply; or fold the scale: float scale = s / len and return new quaternion(axis.x*scale, axis.y*scale, axis.z*scale, c), removing the explicit normalize vector entirely.
perf.rationale: sincos is cheaper than independent sin+cos. Folding 1/len and s into one scalar 'scale' replaces a float3 divide plus a float3 multiply-by-s with a single float3 multiply, cutting the vector op count.
perf.risk: Folding s/len is algebraically identical to (axis/len)*s. The len < Epsilon early-out is preserved. No semantic change.

perf.summary: Half-angle products c.x*c.y, s.x*s.y, etc. recomputed across the four components
perf.currentCost: The four-component construction recomputes shared subproducts: c.x*c.y appears in z and w; s.x*s.y appears in z and w; c.x*s.y, s.x*c.y, c.y*c.z patterns repeat. Each is a separate multiply emitted unless the compiler CSEs aggressively.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute the 6 distinct pair products once: float cxcy=c.x*c.y, sxsy=s.x*s.y, cxsy=c.x*s.y, sxcy=s.x*c.y (and reuse), then build the four outputs from these and the third-axis c.z/s.z. This guarantees CSE rather than relying on the optimizer.
perf.rationale: Reduces the multiply count in the quaternion construction by reusing shared products, shortening the dependency chain feeding the constructor.
perf.risk: Pure algebraic factoring; identical floating-point result if grouped to preserve the original multiply order. Burst likely already CSEs this, so impact is low and mainly a readability/guarantee win.

perf.summary: length+divide pattern can use rsqrt to replace sqrt-then-divide with one reciprocal-sqrt multiply
perf.currentCost: len = math.length(q) does sqrt(dot); then inv = One/len is a divide; then 4 multiplies. That is one sqrt plus one divide on the dependency chain.
perf.proposedChange: Compute float lenSq = math.lengthsq(q.value); guard lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon; inv = math.rsqrt(lenSq); multiply the four components by inv. Replaces sqrt+divide with a single rsqrt.
perf.rationale: rsqrt is a single hardware-friendly op replacing the sqrt then reciprocal-divide sequence, cutting one high-latency divide off the chain.
perf.risk: math.rsqrt may use a lower-precision estimate on some targets, slightly changing the last ULPs of the normalized result versus 1/sqrt. If exact bit-parity with the current sqrt-then-divide is required by tests, keep One/math.sqrt(lenSq) instead (still saves nothing over current). The Epsilon guard must become Epsilon*Epsilon on lenSq to preserve the same cutoff.

perf.summary: normalizesafe(cross) computed before the degenerate-input lengthsq(r) check, and four /s divides per branch
perf.currentCost: r = normalizesafe(cross(up,f)) normalizes r, then math.lengthsq(r) < Epsilon checks degeneracy AFTER normalization. normalizesafe already returns 0 for degenerate cross, so lengthsq(r) is ~0 only when normalizesafe bailed; computing the full normalize then re-measuring its squared length is wasteful. Each of the four trace branches also performs three or four scalar /s divisions.
perf.proposedChange: Compute crossUF = math.cross(up, f); test math.lengthsq(crossUF) < Epsilon BEFORE normalizing to early-out on degenerate input, then r = normalize(crossUF). In each branch replace the repeated '/ s' with a precomputed float invS = One / s and multiply, e.g. (m21 - m12) * invS, and s * Half stays.
perf.rationale: Moves the cheap degeneracy test (lengthsq, no sqrt) ahead of the expensive normalize so degenerate inputs skip normalization entirely; reordering also tests the raw cross magnitude which is the true degeneracy signal rather than the post-normalize length. Replacing 3 divides with 1 reciprocal + 3 multiplies per branch shortens the critical path.
perf.risk: Behavior is preserved only if the degeneracy threshold maps correctly: current code checks lengthsq of the normalized r against Epsilon; checking lengthsq of the raw cross is the more correct degeneracy test but uses a different magnitude scale, so the Epsilon constant for the raw-cross test should be chosen to match intent (raw cross can be tiny yet valid for near-unit inputs). Safer minimal change: keep the normalize but hoist invS in each branch (pure win, no threshold change). The reorder is the higher-impact but threshold-sensitive part.

perf.summary: sinHalf = sqrt(1-w*w) then divide by sinHalf; can be reciprocal-multiply, and acos(w) shares w
perf.currentCost: sinHalf = math.sqrt(One - w*w); then axis = xyz / sinHalf is a float3 divide (3 divides).
perf.proposedChange: Compute float invSin = One / sinHalf once after the Epsilon guard and multiply: axis = new float3(x,y,z) * invSin. Replaces 3 component divides with 1 reciprocal + 3 multiplies.
perf.rationale: Vector divide-by-scalar becomes reciprocal-then-multiply, removing two of the three divide-latency operations.
perf.risk: Algebraically identical; the sinHalf < Epsilon guard already ensures the reciprocal is finite. No semantic change.

perf.summary: Branch for abs() can be branchless math.abs
perf.currentCost: After clamp, an if (d<0) d=-d branch computes absolute value with a conditional, creating a predictable-but-present branch.
perf.proposedChange: Replace the if-block with d = math.abs(d) (or fold: d = math.abs(math.dot(...)) then clamp to [0,1]). Branchless, one instruction.
perf.rationale: math.abs is a single bitwise/instruction op with no branch, removing a conditional from the leaf method that may be called in tight loops (e.g. per-bone angle checks).
perf.risk: math.abs(d) is identical to the if-negate for all finite d. Ordering note: abs-then-clamp to [0,1] is equivalent to clamp[-1,1]-then-abs since abs maps [-1,1] to [0,1]. No semantic change.
